proof:
Use the actual affine hull repair in affine-simplex-first-jets-by-actual-hull-repair. An expanded-simplex enclosure moves its vertices by $O(t^2)$, and its volume differs from the candidate volume by $O(t^2)$, by the simplex determinant formula. Because the actual fibers contain the candidates, the volume change between them bounds the change in any one cap, uniformly over all ambient halfspaces, including moving caps. In particular the repaired total has derivative $M'=\sum_z |K_z|\operatorname{tr}A_z$.

For the candidate affine path, let a row have continuous normal $u\ne0$, old fiber threshold $b_z$, and shifted threshold $b_z+t s$. Pull back to the old fiber under $x\mapsto x+tV_z(x)$. The moving indicator changes its raw volume to first order by
$$
\frac1{\|u\|}\int_{K_z\cap\{u\cdot x=b_z\}}(u\cdot V_z(x)-s)\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)
$$
at a proper trace. To see this, write $x=y+r u/\|u\|$ with $y\perp u$. The changed condition moves the threshold for $r$ by $t(s-u\cdot V_z(y+r_0 u/\|u\|))/\|u\|+O(t^2)$, uniformly on the bounded region, where $r_0=b_z/\|u\|$. For almost every $y$ in the section projection $r_0$ is interior to its line interval, and almost every $y$ outside has no first change. The difference quotients are bounded by the uniform displacement and dominated convergence gives the formula. At a strict full or empty trace the volume indicator is unchanged; at a supporting trace of zero section area the same dominated bound gives zero section term. This also works for proper interval cuts, with the section a single interior point and counting measure. The map's determinant adds $\operatorname{tr}A_z\,|K_z\cap H_z|$. The divergence theorem on $K_z\cap H_z$ cancels its internal cut-face flux against the $u\cdot V_z$ term and leaves the original body-boundary flux, minus $s$ times the section coarea. Full fibers give the whole body-boundary flux and empty fibers give zero.

For each row $j$ let $A_j$ be its summed fixed-cap flux, and $S_j>0$ its summed section area divided by its continuous normal length. The repaired cap with threshold shift $t s_j$ then has raw mass $Q+t(A_j-S_j s_j)+o(t)$. Put $q=(\sum_j\rho_j A_j/S_j)/(\sum_j\rho_j/S_j)$ and set $s_j=(A_j-q)/S_j$. Their weighted sum is zero. Because the original positive linear combination of the margins is nonnegative on the assigned base planes, its sign is preserved there, and at least one row still covers every point of each such plane. This gives common raw response $q$ and after normalization the numerator $q-\beta M'=R(V)$ as stated. If the circuit controls all deepest planes in this sense and finite covers with old strict slack cover the remaining base planes, those margins persist and $R(V)<0$ would strictly lower the actual maximum for small positive $t$. For fixed slack caps their masses are continuous by the same bounded symmetric-difference estimate for affine changes and by repair. Thus a local minimum under these paths implies $R\ge0$ on the feasible cone.

The linear functionals $L_\ell$ define a finite closed polyhedral cone in $E$. Finite Farkas duality says that the linear functionals nonnegative on it are exactly the nonnegative linear combinations of $L_\ell$. This equivalence makes no constraint qualification assumption and applies on the chosen $E$. If $E$ permits independent translations and linear fields at every fiber, compare coefficients of each $c_z$ and $A_z$ in this identity. With the boundary matrices $f_z,B_z$ of the statement this gives
$$
f_z=\sum_{\ell:q=z}\gamma_\ell n_i-\sum_{\ell:z\text{ input}}\gamma_\ell a_z n_i,\qquad
B_z=\sum_{\ell:q=z}\gamma_\ell n_i\xi^{\mathsf T}-\sum_{\ell:z\text{ input}}\gamma_\ell a_z n_i x_z^{\mathsf T}.
$$
The three stated sums vanish label by label, using respectively $\sum_z a_z=1$, $\sum_z a_z x_z=\xi$, and $\sum_z a_z z=q$. These identities compare only the one regular controlling circuit specified above.

statement:
Under affine-simplex-first-jets-by-actual-hull-repair, the added fiber volumes between the actual repaired fibers and their candidate affine images are $O(t^2)$. The change in total volume and in the mass of any fixed or moving ambient closed cap is consequently $O(t^2)$ uniformly in the cap.

Let a fixed regular critical circuit of old mass $Q=\beta M$ per cap have nonzero continuous normals $u_j$, positive balancing coefficients $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, and nonnegative weighted margin on all assigned base planes. Suppose it controls the deepest base planes and finite covers with strict slack cover the others. Assume no positive-area supporting coincidence and that each row has positive total proper coarea $S_j$ (the sum of its proper section areas divided by $\|u_j\|$). Put $\theta_j=(\rho_j/S_j)/\sum_h(\rho_h/S_h)$ and $W_z(x)=\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf 1_{H_j}(z,x)$. The normalized common first cover response times $M$ is
$$
R(V)=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)n\cdot V_z\,dS .
$$
The total first derivative is $\sum_z |K_z|\operatorname{tr}A_z$. A local minimum under these actual paths forces $R\ge0$ on the labeled first-jet cone.

For any linear $R$ on the chosen velocity space, nonnegativity whenever $L_\ell\ge0$ is equivalent to $R=\sum_\ell\gamma_\ell L_\ell$ on that space for some $\gamma_\ell\ge0$. If the velocity space permits all independent affine fields and $R$ has the above boundary profile, put $f_z=\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)n\,dS$ and $B_z=\int_{\partial K_z}(W_z-\beta)nx^{\mathsf T}\,dS$. Each contact label with target $q$, weights $a_z$, normal $n_i$, tuple $x_z$ and mean $\xi$ contributes $\gamma_\ell n_i$ and $\gamma_\ell n_i\xi^{\mathsf T}$ at its target, minus the terms $\gamma_\ell a_z n_i$ and $\gamma_\ell a_z n_i x_z^{\mathsf T}$ at its inputs. In particular $\sum_z f_z=0$, $\sum_z B_z=0$, and $\sum_z f_z z^{\mathsf T}=0$.
title: Regular mixed cap response and labeled affine contact stress
